chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Abī Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who becomes junub during travel and finds nothing but snow. He said: “He performs ghusl with snow or with river water.”

key_terms.الثَّلْجَ: snow used here as the available means for purification
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel; the state of being away from home on a journey
key_terms.مَاءِ النَّهَرِ: river water, mentioned as a valid means for ghusl
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلُ: he performs ghusl, the ritual bath
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: becomes in a state requiring ghusl due to janabah

ai.seo_question: What should a traveler do for ghusl if he becomes junub and only finds snow?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity for a person who becomes junub while traveling and has limited access to water. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that ghusl may be performed with snow or river water, showing the practical application of taharah rulings in difficult travel conditions.
